successCriteria.description: The ILeaveRequestService interface declares submit, approve, reject, cancel, getById, and getByEmployee operations with the actor/approver role threaded as an explicit parameter on every state-changing method.
submit rejects a past startDate and an endDate-before-startDate with a typed validation error before any persistence occurs.
submit enforces the policy's minimumNoticeDays (when defined and > 0) against the gap between today and startDate, throwing a typed validation error when the notice is insufficient.
submit computes requested leave days via countBusinessDays with an empty holidays array, and rejects a range that spans zero business days with a typed validation error.

submit recomputes remaining balance inline as totalEntitlement - usedDays (not trusting a stored remainingDays field) and throws InsufficientBalanceError when the computed remaining is less than the requested business days.
submit atomically increments usedDays on the LeaveBalance before/with persisting the request, and the resulting LeaveRequest has status SUBMITTED.
submit does NOT auto-approve a request for a manager-less employee (managerId null); the request remains SUBMITTED and requires hr_admin approval.
approve sets status to APPROVED with approvedBy and approvedAt populated, and does NOT modify usedDays on the LeaveBalance.
approve authorizes only the employee's direct manager (approverId === employee.managerId) or, when managerId is null, only hr_admin; any other approver throws ApproverNotAuthorizedError.
reject applies the same authorization rule as approve, sets status to REJECTED, and restores usedDays on the LeaveBalance (floored at zero) using the recomputed business days.

cancel is permitted only when the prior status is SUBMITTED or APPROVED (other statuses throw a typed validation error); an employee may cancel only their own request while manager/hr_admin may cancel any.
cancel restores usedDays on the LeaveBalance only when the prior status was SUBMITTED; cancelling an APPROVED request does NOT touch usedDays.
getById returns the LeaveRequest or null, and getByEmployee returns the array of the employee's requests (empty array when none), delegating to the repository without authorization logic.

The barrel export (index.ts) re-exports the service interface, the service class, and the four typed error classes (InsufficientBalanceError, ApproverNotAuthorizedError, ValidationError, LeaveRequestNotFoundError).

The Jest test suite covers each method's happy path and error paths: insufficient balance, unauthorized approver, past startDate, endDate-before-startDate, insufficient notice, zero business days, missing employee/policy/balance, not-found request, wrong-status approve/reject/cancel, and cross-employee cancel — all using mocked repository dependencies.

constraints: All database access goes through repository interfaces (GP-001); the service must not import or call the pg Pool, connection, or any repository implementation class directly — only the ILeaveRequestRepository, ILeaveBalanceRepository, IEmployeeRepository, and ILeavePolicyRepository interfaces.
RBAC is enforced inside the service via the explicit actorRole/approverRole parameter (GP-005); the service must not read ambient auth state, and the role is never inferred from the Employee entity.
No use of any (HARNESS no-any rule); use unknown with type guards where dynamic values are handled.
remainingDays must never be written or trusted as a stored value; it is always recomputed inline as totalEntitlement - usedDays at the point of the balance-sufficiency check.
Business-day counting must use the shared countBusinessDays utility with an empty holidays array, comparing dates by UTC-midnight calendar-date equality (exclusive of the end day).
fiscalYear is derived as the calendar year of the request's startDate (UTC), not from a tenant configuration or a separate field.
Test files must use the *.test.ts convention under tests/ with jest.Mocked<Interface> and manual jest.fn() per method in beforeEach; no jest.mock() factory for service tests.
Modules import from each other only through their declared public entry point (index.ts); no imports of another module's internal files.
outOfScope: Audit logging (GP-002 audit records) — deferred to Phase 9 (audit-log module) and Phase 10 (integration into LeaveRequestService).
Notification dispatch (LEAVE_APPLIED / LEAVE_DECISION / BALANCE_LOW) — deferred to Phase 9 (notification module) and Phase 10 (integration).
Fastify controller and routes (HTTP methods, paths, request.user consumption, GP-003 boundary validation) — Phase 8.
LeavePolicyService and LeaveBalanceService implementations — Phase 10; this phase consumes only the repository interfaces and the LeaveBalance service interface shape.
Public-holiday calendar / holidays table integration — countBusinessDays is called with an empty holidays array in this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle is strictly DRAFT → SUBMITTED → (APPROVED | REJECTED) → CANCELLED; approve and reject operate only on a SUBMITTED request, and cancel operates only on a SUBMITTED or APPROVED request — any other source status is rejected with a typed validation error.

usedDays is the denormalized source of truth: incremented atomically on submit, restored (floored at zero) on reject and on cancel-of-SUBMITTED, and untouched on approve and on cancel-of-APPROVED; remainingDays is always derived as totalEntitlement - usedDays and never persisted or trusted as stored.
A null managerId escalates approval authority to hr_admin only — the service must neither auto-approve nor permit a manager to approve/reject a manager-less employee's request.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: An employee actor may submit only for themselves (actorId === dto.employeeId); manager and hr_admin actors may submit for any employee.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Typed errors: ApproverNotAuthorizedError (employee submitting for another), ValidationError (past startDate, endDate before startDate, insufficient notice, zero business days, missing employee/policy/balance), InsufficientBalanceError (remaining < requested days).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Approver must be the employee's direct manager (approverId === employee.managerId) OR, when managerId is null, approverRole must be hr_admin; hr_admin may not approve when a manager exists, and a manager may not approve when managerId is null.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Typed errors: LeaveRequestNotFoundError (no request), ValidationError (status not SUBMITTED, missing employee), ApproverNotAuthorizedError (wrong approver/role). Does not modify usedDays.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Same authorization rule as approve: employee's direct manager, or hr_admin when managerId is null.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Typed errors: LeaveRequestNotFoundError, ValidationError (status not SUBMITTED, missing employee), ApproverNotAuthorizedError. Restores usedDays (floored at zero) using recomputed business days; missing balance is tolerated (no update, no error).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: An employee actor may cancel only their own request (actorId === leaveRequest.employeeId); manager and hr_admin actors may cancel any request.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Typed errors: LeaveRequestNotFoundError, ValidationError (prior status not SUBMITTED or APPROVED), ApproverNotAuthorizedError (employee cancelling another's request). Restores usedDays only when prior status was SUBMITTED; missing balance is tolerated.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No authorization enforced in the service for these read operations (RBAC for reads is applied at the controller/middleware layer in Phase 8).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: getById returns LeaveRequest | null; getByEmployee returns LeaveRequest[] (empty array when none). Pure delegation to the repository; no typed errors thrown for not-found.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Business-day counting in the service must call the shared countBusinessDays(startDate, endDate, []) utility and rely on its exclusive-end, UTC-midnight semantics — the service must not re-implement day counting.
Status transitions must use the LeaveRequestStatus enum members (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) imported from the shared-types barrel — no string literals for status.

The service must call only the ILeaveRequestRepository operations (findById, findByEmployee, create, updateStatus) as declared in Phase 6; the create→updateStatus(SUBMITTED) sequence must match the repository's contract where create persists with DRAFT status.

Balance lookups and mutations must use ILeaveBalanceRepository.findByEmployeeAndPolicy(employeeId, leavePolicyId, fiscalYear) and updateUsedDays(id, usedDays) as declared in Phase 5; the service recomputes remaining inline rather than reading the repository's derived remainingDays property.

The service must operate on the LeaveRequest and CreateLeaveRequestDto shapes defined in Phase 6, setting approvedBy/approvedAt on approve and reject and leaving them null on submit/cancel per the model contract.

The barrel export must re-export the service interface, the service class, and all four typed error classes so downstream phases (controller, audit integration) import only through the public entry point.

integrationPoints.why: submit increments usedDays, reject and cancel-of-SUBMITTED restore usedDays via findByEmployeeAndPolicy + updateUsedDays.
submit looks up the LeavePolicy by id to read minimumNoticeDays and validate the policy exists.
submit, approve, and reject look up the Employee to verify existence and read managerId for authorization/escalation.
submit, reject, and cancel compute requested/restored business days via the shared utility with an empty holidays array.
Phase 8 controller consumes this interface to delegate all leave-request operations, passing request.user.id and request.user.role as actor parameters.

Phase 10 will inject IAuditService and INotificationService into LeaveRequestService to emit audit records and notifications on submit/approve/reject/cancel — the current service must remain structured to accept these additions without rewriting the business logic.
